• Common name: Armoured sea catfish
  • Synonyms: Cephalocassis stormii, Arius stormii, Tachysurus stormii
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (IUCN 2020)
Asia: Thailand to Indonesia. Type locality: Sumatra (Palembang), in flumine Mussi.
Occurs in medium to large-sized rivers and feeds mainly on invertebrates and small fishes.
In most, if not all species, the male carries the relatively large eggs in its mouth until hatching.

Description: Differs from other species of the family in Laos by having the head wider than deep. Pointed snout with conspicuous inferior mouth. Granulated palatine teeth.

Etymology: The specific name stormii honours F. J. P. Storm van 's Gravesande (1812-1875), Dutch government commissioner of Djambi (also spelled Jambi), Sumatra, who provided the type.

IUCN Red List: Although there is no detailed information on the population size and trend of this species, there is currently no evidence that the population is in significant decline; its trend is thus suspected to be stable or declining at a rate that precludes it from being assessed in a threatened category. While there may be localised or regional threats, they are unlikely to affect this species on a range-wide scale. Therefore, Hemiarius stormii is assessed as Least Concern (IUCN 2020).
